title: Lean 4 for Reward Hacking Detection: Can Formal Specs Capture Reward Function Properties?

original_idea.body:
# Lean 4 for Reward Hacking Detection: Can Formal Specs Capture Reward Function Properties?

**Problem:** Reward hacking (RL agents exploiting reward function misspecification) is a core AI safety problem. Whether formal specifications can express and verify properties of reward functions that prevent common hacking patterns is unexplored.

**Direction:** Model 5 simple RL environments in Lean 4. Write formal reward function specifications that explicitly exclude known reward hacking patterns (e.g., 'reward must not increase when episode is prematurely terminated'). Test whether LLMs can generate these specs and proofs.

**Why it matters:** Formally verified reward functions would provide mathematical guarantees against certain classes of reward hacking. Even partial coverage would be a meaningful advance in RL safety grounded in formal methods.

**Relevant context:** Reward hacking is a central AI safety concern (Sutton & Barto, Amodei et al.). Formal verification of reward functions is not attempted in current literature. Lean 4's expressive type system could capture reward properties as types.
